children: By Sukanya Mitra

Gold prices ticked lower on Wednesday after the previous session's climb of about 1%, as higher oil prices stoked inflation fears while investors awaited the Federal Reserve's policy decision later in the day for clues to the rate outlook.
Spot gold
was down 0.7% at $4,030.20 per ounce by 0602 GMT. US gold futures
for December delivery dropped 0.8% to $4,043.0.
"Gold is moving based on the interest rate expectations and inflation risks because of higher energy prices," said Soni Kumari, an analyst at ANZ.
"As a result, the Fed will remain cautious, which remains a short-term key headwind for gold."
Oil prices climbed more than 1% on Wednesday after an attack on a refinery in Saudi Arabia renewed concerns around supply risks from the major exporter.
Elevated energy prices raise expectations that the Fed will keep interest rates higher for longer, increasing the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion.

Markets await the Fed's policy decision due at 1800 GMT, along with the Personal Consumption Expenditures data on Thursday, a key gauge closely watched by the central bank as it targets a 2% inflation rate.
Traders largely expect the Fed to leave rates unchanged today but are pricing in a chance of about 84% for a December rate hike, according to the CME's FedWatch Tool.
High inflation will persist in the global economy well into next year, according to hundreds of economists polled by Reuters.

Meanwhile, analysts cut their 2026 gold price forecast for a second straight quarter due to high Treasury yields, a strong US dollar and expectations that rates will stay higher for longer, but still expect a recovery in 2027, a Reuters survey showed.
Additionally, analysts and traders cut their platinum and palladium price forecasts for 2026 for a third straight quarter, a Reuters survey showed.
Among other metals, spot silver
slid 1% to $53.82 per ounce, platinum
lost 0.9% to $1,526.74 and palladium
steadied at $1,025.63.
